cs.t: Specifically, emulators work best with the real controller. And feature sets across controllers are not 1:1. Like, a Switch Pro has an accelerometer and is used in Zelda games. I have a switch pro for switch games. I have a dualshock ps4 controller for PS/PS2/PS3/PS4/PS5 I have a steam controller as well for non-emulated games with Steam.

Their hardware quality is definitely sub-par. I got the Pro Controller because the joycons are The Worst [1], and it's definitely the worst quality controller compared to Xbox and PS4. For example, its D-Pad will occasionally mis-press up or down when pressing right or left, which is failing the basic purpose of a D-Pad. That said, the concept of the Switch remains fantastic, and I take it with me whenever I travel. I'm definitely in line for getting the Steam Deck.
